transcript:
User: Hey! So I'm Sofia — I run a real estate office here in Houston. Your ad was talking about missed calls? That's literally me.
Agent: Mhm, got it Sofia — you saw our ad about “missed calls.” What’s making the missed calls a problem for you right now?
User: Well, I don't track it, but maybe 25? Or 30? Losing clients, need help to manage it.
Agent: Yeah, that’s a lot — if you miss a call, do those clients usually leave a voicemail, or do they just move on to the next agent?
User: Honestly, they probably just move on. Voicemails? Rarely. I need a solution fast. What's your service about?
Agent: Got it — and yeah, in real estate if they don’t leave a voicemail, they’re usually calling the next agent.

Dialux makes sure those inbound calls get answered and captured even when you’re tied up: we respond right away, qualify what they need, and get them booked or routed so you stop losing clients. About how many inbound calls a week do you think are hitting voicemail right now — 10, 20, 30?
User: I don't track that... maybe 25? Or 30? Yes, tell me more — this is exactly what I need!
Agent: Makes sense — we can use 30 as a working number. Of those missed calls, what percentage do you think would turn into a client or appointment if you actually answered—half?
User: Yeah, maybe half. Maybe more! I really need to stop missing these calls. Can you help with that?
Agent: Yeah, we can absolutely help with that. What’s your average commission or value per closed client—are we talking $2,000, $5,000, $10,000?
User: Oh, it's around $5,000 per closed client. So, you can see why missing calls is a huge problem!
Agent: Yeah… so if you booked even 50% of those 30 missed calls, that’s about **$75000 extra a week**—and that’s just one week, about **$324700/mo** over a month. Does that sound about right?
User: Wow! That would be amazing. If this service helps, I need to start yesterday. Tell me more!
Agent: Totally hear you — with that kind of money on the line, moving fast makes sense. It’s a 20‑minute walkthrough where Jay shows exactly how it works and what it would look like on your calls; what’s better for you — later today or tomorrow?
User: Actually, tomorrow works! But wait, let's confirm the time again; I changed the day. Can we re-confirm?
Agent: Got it — tomorrow works. Before we lock a time, what’s your last name?
User: Oh! It's Sofia Martinez. Let's make sure the time's right though. You're in Mountain, right? Oh, sorry, Central!
Agent: Got it — Central time. Is the number you’re calling from the best contact number for the SMS confirmation?
User: Yes, this number is perfect for the SMS confirmation. Just double-check the time for tomorrow, okay?
Agent: Got it — I’ll use this number. Quick check: you’re in **Houston on Central time**, right?
User: Yes, I'm in Houston, Central time. Let's confirm the time again for tomorrow. Just want to be sure!
Agent: Perfect — Houston, Central time. What time tomorrow works best for you: morning or afternoon?
User: Afternoon works best. Can we do 2 PM Central? Please confirm that's set for tomorrow. Thanks!
Agent: 2 PM Central works on your end—what day tomorrow is that for you (e.g., Tuesday), just so I line it up correctly?
User: Yes, 2 PM Central tomorrow, which is Tuesday. Let's lock that in! Thanks for your patience.
Agent: Got it — I can’t do **2:00 PM** tomorrow, but I *can* do **1:45 PM** or **2:30 PM** Central; which one do you want?
User: Let's do 2:30 PM Central tomorrow. Please confirm the time again for me, just in case!
Agent: So that’s **tomorrow, Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central**, correct? Quick thing - what's the best number to reach you on?
User: Yes, tomorrow at 2:30 PM Central. Call me at [your phone number]. Thanks for confirming!
Agent: Got it — tomorrow (Tuesday) at **2:30 PM Central**. Oh sorry, I didn't get your number quite right - could you verify it real quick?
User: Sure, it's [your phone number]. Please make sure we're set for 2:30 PM Central tomorrow. Thanks!
Agent: Got it — and yes, I have **Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central**. Oh sorry, I didn't get your number quite right - could you verify it real quick (just read the digits to me)?
User: Sure, my number is 555-123-4567. Thanks for confirming the time on Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Got it — thanks. The calendar’s rejecting the booking because it’s flagging the phone number format; can you confirm it as **+1** then the number (for example **+15551234567**)?
User: Great, thank you! Just let me know when it's confirmed. I'm really excited to get started with this!
Agent: Totally hear you — I’m excited for you too. I can’t confirm it yet because the calendar is still rejecting the phone number format; can you text me the number exactly as **+1** plus the 10 digits (example: **+15551234567**) so I can lock the **Tuesday 2:30 PM Central** slot?
User: Sure, I'll text you right now: +15551234567. Please confirm once it's locked for Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central. Thanks!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Got it — thanks. The calendar’s still rejecting **+15551234567** as “invalid,” so I can’t confirm the Tuesday 2:30 PM Central booking yet; what’s the best alternate number (include country code) I should use instead?
User: Great, thanks! Just want to make sure we're all set. Looking forward to the call!
Agent: I’m not able to say we’re set yet — the calendar is still rejecting the booking because it’s flagging the phone number as invalid. What’s the best alternate number to use (with country code) so I can lock Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central?
User: Oh, my bad! Use +15559876543 instead. Please confirm once Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central is booked. Thanks!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Got it — the calendar’s still rejecting that number as “invalid,” so I can’t confirm Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central yet. Is that a US mobile number that can receive SMS, or is there another number you want me to try?
User: Perfect, I'll wait. Just let me know when it's all set. Can't wait to get started!
Agent: I hear you — I just can’t confirm it yet because the calendar is still rejecting every number as “invalid,” so it won’t let me lock Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central. What email should I attach to the invite instead?
User: Oh, that's odd! Use my email: sofia@houstonhomes.com. Please confirm once it's locked for Tuesday, 2:30 PM Central.
Agent: Thanks — I’ve got **sofia@houstonhomes.com**. I still can’t confirm the booking yet because the calendar is rejecting the phone number field, but I can try again using your email attached; is it okay if I use **+15551234567** as the phone on the invite?
User: Yes, use +15551234567 for the invite. Please confirm once it's booked for Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Got it — the calendar is still rejecting the booking because it keeps flagging the phone number as invalid, so I can’t confirm **Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central** yet. Would you rather do **1:45 PM** or **3:15 PM** Central instead?
User: Sure, I'll wait. Just want to ensure we're all set for Tuesday, 2:30 PM Central.
Agent: Got it — I’m not able to confirm Tuesday at 2:30 PM Central because the calendar keeps rejecting the booking, so let’s pick a nearby time I can lock in. Please tell me whether 1:45 PM or 3:15 PM Central works better, and I’ll book it right then. Thanks, Sofia.
